newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver dips on large arrivals, gold subdued.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver dips on large arrivals, gold subdued.

text.p: Silver prices closed lower on higher arrivals on Thursday after opening lower on the back of overnight losses in the world market, dealers said.
Silver was down by 55 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
The market was closed on Wednesday for New Year holiday.
About 1,000/1,200 kg of the imported silver arrived in the Bombay market on Thursday. Industrial buying was sluggish.

Gold prices opened lower on news that government doubled the quantity of gold that can be brought into the country by non-resident Indians to 10 kg, but prices were steady at the opening level throughout the day amid limited activity.
Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) settled 400 rupees lower at 58,700 rupees per piece. They were down by 200 rupees per piece on Tuesday.

"Though government has liberalised gold import, traders were expecting limited arrivals in the coming days as local prices are still at discount compared to the landing cost of imported gold," said Babubhai Jain, a leading jeweller.
"The margins are not much attractive to bring gold into India," he said.
